articles.author: ellis-quill
articles.title: Just a cactus, fifty-one yards, and a division for Lavender
articles.dek: The Wails turn fourteen seconds into a championship finish: two completions, one field goal and a 21–20 win over Blackthorn.

body.text: Lavender had fourteen seconds and a division to recover. Blackthorn’s Cacturne had just made a 48-yard field goal, moving the Dragons ahead 20–18 and putting the Johto East title back within their reach. The kickoff left the Wails at their own 29. Moth Ball needed to move them far enough for one more kick, and he had very little time in which to decide what far enough might mean.

He found Sly Cooper for nineteen yards down the left side, out of bounds, with ten seconds showing. He found People Eater for eighteen more through the middle with six. Just a cactus came on for a 51-yard field goal. The kick was good at 0:02. Lavender won 21–20, finished 12–5 and took the division from the team that had arrived needing only a win or tie to retain it. Blackthorn finished with the same record and a road trip to Cinnabar.

The Wails will host Vermilion as the third seed. That is the practical consequence of a finish that invited considerably less practical behavior from anyone watching. Travis Scarboro’s team had been behind 10–0, had tied the game, had fallen behind again, had taken an 18–17 lead, and then had watched Blackthorn restore its advantage. Lavender’s season came down to whether two completions could create a final attempt. They did, and the kicker completed the work.

I have watched this team win eight straight now. The sequence began after a 17–7 loss at Pastoria left the Wails 4–5. Some victories were narrow, some required late offense, and the 51–10 win at Violet suggested a passing game becoming more dangerous. The division finale required the full range of that recent education. Lavender needed patience through a poor start, production when the field became urgent and a final kick that did not care how much the standings had attached to it.
The fourth down that kept the division available
We needed the first down. Then we needed the conversion. Then we needed enough yards for the kick. We did those things. We will look at the rest of it.
body.speaker: Travis Scarboro

body.text: The final kick was possible because Lavender had already rescued an earlier possession. Blackthorn led 17–10 after Hatterene’s one-yard touchdown run at 3:04 of the fourth quarter. The Wails reached third-and-four near the two-minute warning, then Moth Ball missed Unfezant on a short pass to the right. Fourth down followed with 1:56 remaining. A failure there would have left the Dragons ahead with the ball and the division close at hand.

Moth Ball threw short left to The Wail for eight yards and a first down. It was the kind of conversion that can disappear beneath the more spectacular events afterward, although this ending depends on it. Samurott caught the next two passes, eight yards through the middle and twelve to the right for a touchdown at 1:41. Lavender had closed to 17–16 and chose to pursue the lead immediately. Machoke ran up the middle for the two-point conversion.

body.alt: Frosmoth #15, Wailord #99. Moth Ball found Wail for eight yards on fourth-and-four in the late touchdown drive. Editorial illustration of the recorded play.
body.caption: Moth Ball found Wail for eight yards on fourth-and-four in the late touchdown drive. Editorial illustration of the recorded play.

body.text: That choice made the score 18–17. It also left Blackthorn enough time to answer. Hatterene used Furret’s rushing gains and completions to Grovyle and Meganium to move the Dragons into range. A third-and-one throw toward Sharpedo was incomplete at 0:22, and Cacturne made the 48-yarder five seconds later. Blackthorn had handled the pressure of the possession well enough to retake the lead. Lavender then handled an even smaller remaining window.

The two teams produced an ending in which both offenses had a credible claim to having done their job. Hatterene finished 23 of 30 for 301 yards, one passing touchdown and one interception, adding a rushing touchdown. Moth Ball went 25 of 37 for 248 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions. The difference was the last pair of completions and the kick they enabled. An accurate afternoon for Hatterene did not leave the Dragons with the last meaningful possession.
Lavender recovered from its own missed chances

The first half gave the Wails several reasons to be frustrated. Hatterene hit Ninjask for a seven-yard touchdown on the first play of the second quarter. Moth Ball then completed a thirty-yard pass to People Eater, who fumbled, with Blastoise recovering for Blackthorn. The Dragons added Cacturne’s 34-yard field goal and led 10–0. Lavender finally scored on a 31-yard field goal with one second left before halftime.

That late first-half kick mattered to the arithmetic as much as the last one. Just a cactus finished two for two on field goals and made the one conventional extra point Lavender attempted. The Wails did not leave kicking points behind while the offense worked through its uneven start. Hobbes then supplied a one-yard rushing touchdown in the third quarter, completing the recovery to 10–10.

Picasso gave the defense its defining takeaway. With 1:19 left in the third, Hatterene’s deep pass to the right was intercepted and returned twenty-five yards by the Lavender cornerback. It was Blackthorn’s second giveaway after Furret’s first-quarter fumble, recovered by Blathers. The Wails lost one fumble of their own. Those possessions helped keep the game within reach even though Blackthorn finished with 367 total yards to Lavender’s 348.

body.alt: Frosmoth #15, Maractus #12. Moth Ball and Just a cactus supplied the passing and kicking work in Lavender’s final drive. An imagined postgame portrait.
body.caption: Moth Ball and Just a cactus supplied the passing and kicking work in Lavender’s final drive. An imagined postgame portrait.

body.text: Lavender did enough in the running game to keep Moth Ball’s work connected to a broader offense. Hobbes carried fourteen times for eighty-six yards and the touchdown. Machoke added fourteen yards on three carries, with the successful two-point run recorded separately. The Wails finished with one hundred rushing yards, compared with Blackthorn’s sixty-six. Their seventeen first downs also exceeded the Dragons’ twelve.

That production did not make the afternoon comfortable. Lavender punted four times and converted four of ten third downs. Blackthorn punted twice and went four of nine. The Wails still needed their fourth-down conversion, the aggressive two-point decision and the final field goal. This was a victory assembled from several necessary answers, rather than a dominant statistical performance waiting for the score to agree with it.

The distribution of the final drive deserves to remain visible beside the kick. Sly Cooper gained nineteen yards and reached the boundary; People Eater followed with eighteen through the middle. Each completion supplied a different requirement. The first bought field position while preserving time, and the second moved the attempt into the distance Just a cactus converted. Moth Ball had to make both throws with the division changing hands behind every incomplete result.

That sequence also explains why the ending should not erase the earlier offensive difficulty. Lavender needed fourth-and-four before it could reach the touchdown, then still needed another possession after Blackthorn’s field goal. The Wails did not control every phase of the closing minutes. They completed the next available task often enough to regain the lead twice. Against Vermilion, a team accustomed to close finishes of its own, Scarboro will want the same precision with fewer occasions requiring it.
Moth Ball’s job keeps getting larger

Moth Ball has become central to the Wails’ late-season identity while Mr. Clanky remains unavailable. The current injury report lists five weeks for the former passing option. Lavender’s response has been to continue building the offense around the players it can use. Unfezant caught seven passes for sixty-nine yards in the finale. People Eater had four for fifty-six, The Wail six for fifty-two and Sly Cooper four for thirty-six.

The distribution matters because the decisive sequence asked different receivers to do different jobs. The Wail converted fourth down. Samurott scored the late touchdown. Sly Cooper provided the out-of-bounds completion that preserved the last attempt, and People Eater supplied the final gain after his earlier fumble. Moth Ball did not need to force every urgent throw toward the same target. Lavender had enough functioning choices to keep using the field.

Blackthorn has its own immediate adjustment to make. The Dragons now visit Cinnabar, which beat them 31–19 in Week 15. Hatterene’s passing can keep that game competitive, but a fifty-sack regular season and the four-week absence still reported for Sawsbuck remain consequential. The finale showed the Dragons capable of moving the ball against a division rival. It also showed how little margin a one-point game leaves for an opponent’s final possession.

Lavender gets Vermilion at home. The Volts won their last three games and generally prefer a lower score than the Wails produced at Violet. Scarboro will have a different set of corrections to make after this one: the early fumble, the four punts, the occasions on which Blackthorn moved the ball efficiently. A division title does not remove those items from the film. It gives the Wails another home game in which to address them, because Moth Ball found thirty-seven yards and Just a cactus supplied fifty-one more.

art.alt: Maractus #12. Just a cactus made a fifty-one-yard field goal to win Johto East. Illustrated from the recorded finish.

articles.author: mara-voss
articles.title: Seventeen wins, and Dorrill still has four sacks to discuss
articles.dek: Budew Baker throws three touchdowns, Shawn Mareman runs for 153 and Mossdeep finishes its perfect regular season with a 27–0 shutout.

body.text: Michael Dorrill reached the end of a 17–0 regular season with a shutout, three touchdown passes from his developmental quarterback and enough offensive mistakes to keep the review meeting occupied. Mossdeep beat Lavaridge 27–0. Budew Baker went 14 of 22 for 157 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions. He was also sacked four times. Anyone expecting Dorrill to skip that last line because the first ones look pleasant has not been listening.

The Eclipse entered the finale with the first seed already secured and a confirmed coaching purpose: rest starters, reduce their injury exposure and give younger players experience. This was the second consecutive start in which Baker helped carry out that plan. He threw two touchdown passes against Sootopolis in the previous week’s 22–3 win, then added three at Lavaridge. Mossdeep’s closing development work produced two wins without asking the young quarterback to reproduce Dram Marino’s season-long output.

Shawn Mareman gave him a substantial running game. The Rapidash carried twenty-four times for 153 yards, caught two passes for fourteen and scored on a five-yard reception. Mossdeep finished with 203 rushing yards and 360 total yards. Lavaridge managed nineteen rushing yards and 132 in all. A team can change important participants and still control the basic terms of an afternoon. The Eclipse did exactly that here.

The defense made the score possible. Derrat Brooks had four sacks, Ninjaskamara added two, and Lavaridge lost forty yards on those six takedowns. The Inferno converted two of nine third downs and punted seven times. Electric Berry recovered the one lost fumble. Mossdeep held the ball through enough productive possessions that Lavaridge had little room to recover from its unsuccessful ones.
Mareman gave Baker useful choices

Four sacks. Two punts. A missed kick. We are going to enjoy the win, and then we are going to understand why those possessions did not finish the way we prepared them to finish. Seventeen wins earns us the next game.
body.speaker: Michael Dorrill

body.text: Mareman’s 153 yards came without a rushing touchdown, which makes the performance a useful reminder to read beyond the scoring column. He averaged 6.4 yards a carry and kept giving the offense gains that did not require another pass. Marshall Flock added twenty-six yards on six carries, and Ninjulio Jones gained twenty-four on two. Mossdeep had thirty-two rushing attempts, enough to make the running game a sustained part of the win.

Baker’s first touchdown went to Driflon Diggs on a one-yard pass short left with 1:41 remaining in the second quarter. Adam Vinathorn’s extra point made it 13–0. The Eclipse had already received two 46-yard field goals from their kicker. Their early points came in pieces while the defense prevented Lavaridge from finding any answer. That was a suitable environment for a quarterback getting meaningful work before the playoffs.

body.alt: Rapidash #21. Shawn Mareman rushed for 153 yards on twenty-four carries. An editorial rushing illustration.
body.caption: Shawn Mareman rushed for 153 yards on twenty-four carries. An editorial rushing illustration.

body.text: The next touchdown came on third-and-five with 1:56 left in the third. Baker threw to Mareman for five yards and the score. Mareman had already done substantial work on the ground. This time he finished the possession as a receiver.

Jones supplied the final touchdown on a twenty-five-yard pass through the middle with 3:37 left in the fourth. He finished with six catches for eighty-three yards, leading Mossdeep’s receivers. Diggs caught four for forty-nine and the earlier score. Will Shells added an eight-yard reception, and George Kipple caught one for three. Baker distributed his fourteen completions across five receivers without throwing an interception.

The clean interception column is encouraging. The protection still needs attention. Baker lost twenty-five yards on four sacks, including consecutive second-quarter takedowns that turned second-and-ten into a much longer situation. The game record identifies the tacklers, but it does not justify assigning every failure to a particular Mossdeep blocker. Dorrill can demand correction without a columnist inventing an individual missed assignment.
Brooks repeatedly ended Lavaridge’s possibilities

Derrat Brooks opened his sack total in the first quarter, taking Delphox down for seven yards. He added another six-yard loss early in the second. The two fourth-quarter sacks were particularly restrictive: seven yards at 4:57 and another seven at 4:44. Lavaridge was already behind 20–0, and those plays made an attempt to revive the game much harder.

Ninjaskamara contributed two sacks for seven yards each, one late in the third quarter and one in the fourth. His presence in the defensive record is worth stating carefully. The veteran’s regular-season rest context does not mean he took no part in this game. The actual box score credits the two sacks and a tackle for loss. Mossdeep’s personnel use was broader than a simple division between eleven resting veterans and eleven young replacements.

body.alt: Raticate #54. Derrat Brooks recorded four sacks in the shutout. An editorial pass-rush collage.
body.caption: Derrat Brooks recorded four sacks in the shutout. An editorial pass-rush collage.

body.text: Electric Berry recovered Fearow’s fumble after a twenty-yard completion on Lavaridge’s first offensive play of the second quarter. That was the game’s only lost fumble, and neither quarterback threw an interception. Mossdeep’s defensive control therefore came largely through stopping ordinary possessions, with one takeaway helping. The Inferno gained six first downs and completed ten of nineteen passes for 113 yards.

The Eclipse allowed no points in any quarter. Lavaridge had a chance to create a different game when Mossdeep’s early drives ended in kicks rather than touchdowns, but its own offense could not extend enough possessions. Seven punts and two successful third downs explain the repeated return of the ball to Baker and Mareman. Mossdeep’s defense supplied the conditions in which its developmental offense could keep trying the next useful thing.

The contrast between the teams’ rushing work explains much of Baker’s opportunity. Mareman could keep a possession usable without requiring a difficult completion on every down. Lavaridge gained nineteen rushing yards across the entire game, leaving its passing offense to recover ground against a defense that repeatedly reached the quarterback. That difference helped Mossdeep convert seven of twelve third downs while the Inferno converted two of nine.

Baker still had his own corrections. Four sacks cost twenty-five yards, and two possessions ended in punts. Dorrill’s confirmed development intent makes those snaps part of the value of the afternoon: the younger quarterback experienced successful scoring work and possessions that stalled against a real opponent. A three-touchdown total supplies encouragement, while the recorded losses give the next review something specific to address. The win does not require describing every developmental snap as a finished skill.
The perfect record belongs beside the preparation

Mossdeep finished the regular season with 724 points scored and 130 allowed, a differential of 594. The Eclipse won all six division games and every other game on the schedule. Their narrowest victories came against Dewford, 24–21, and Saffron, 20–17. Those opponents provided evidence that the postseason can demand a close finish even from the team with the strongest season totals.

Dorrill’s decision to use the closing weeks for rest and experience should shape how those final scores are interpreted. Twenty-two points against Sootopolis and twenty-seven at Lavaridge were produced by the participants actually used. They are not a measurement of the maximum scoring capacity of Marino, Accel BeckhmJr and the established offense. They are evidence that Mossdeep could pursue a different preparation objective and still finish both games with considerable control.

There are availability details to carry forward. Mareman received a minor game injury entry, while the current roster has no positive-week absence for him. That does not by itself establish a future starting role. Poury Holt remains out with six weeks reported after his previous injury. The available backfield options have just demonstrated useful production, but a playoff lineup still needs to be judged when it is confirmed.

The first-round bye means Mossdeep will next host the lowest surviving Hoenn–Sinnoh seed. Its possible opponent depends on six other clubs settling the wild-card round. The Eclipse have earned the extra preparation time. Baker’s two starts, Mareman’s rushing afternoon and the work given to younger defenders provide the staff with more recent evidence about the players behind its established starters.

I would expect Dorrill to begin that preparation with the four sacks, the two punts and the missed field goal. Vinathorn finished two of three on field goals and three of three on extra points. Mossdeep converted seven of twelve third downs, which is productive and still leaves five failures to examine. The coach can acknowledge seventeen wins while insisting that the next opponent will punish wasted possessions more severely. This finale gave him a perfect record and several specific things to coach.

art.alt: Roselia #37, Rapidash #21. Budew Baker and Shawn Mareman helped Mossdeep finish 17–0. An imagined postgame scene.
